title: Squash, bend, twist, stretch
_map: Squash, bend, twist, stretch (Y2). Big idea: some materials change shape when pushed. Creative: test materials with the robot's hands; design a bouncy material for the trampoline.
_story: The robot wants a trampoline. It tests materials by squashing, bending, twisting and stretching them. A metal trampoline would hurt!
_stepChain: materials (whats-it-made-of) → pushing and pulling can change shape → squash, bend, twist, stretch → some spring back (elastic), some stay changed, some don't change → test → the robot's metal trampoline

talk.ask: What's a good material for a trampoline? Why?
talk.goodAnswer: something stretchy that springs back, like rubber or elastic fabric.
things like sponge, play dough, a pillow. Not a stone or a metal spoon.

handsOn: Test some things: a sponge, an elastic band, play dough, a spoon. Can you squash, bend, twist or stretch each one? Does it go back to its shape?

narration.speaker: robot
narration.text: I want to build a trampoline! I need a material that bounces. Let's test some.
Try squashing a sponge: it springs back. Stretch an elastic band: it springs back too. Squash play dough: it stays squashed. A stone won't change shape at all.
A material that stretches or squashes, then springs back to its shape, is called elastic.

narration.speaker: robot
narration.text: I'll make my trampoline out of metal. Metal is really strong!

question.prompt: Is metal good for a trampoline?
question.onRight: Yes, you thought about the job. A trampoline needs to stretch and spring back. Metal doesn't stretch: ouch!

0.mistake: picked strength when the job needs stretch
0.hint: Does metal stretch and spring back when you jump?
0.say: Metal is strong, but it doesn't stretch. You'd land with a bump! A trampoline needs an elastic material that stretches and springs back.

question.reveal: An elastic material makes a bouncy trampoline.

rule.ask: Can you say what elastic means? Say it out loud. Then tap the eye.
rule.spoken: Some materials change shape when you squash, bend, twist or stretch them. Elastic ones spring back to their shape.

bonus.prompt: Bonus: why do bike tyres have air inside?
choices: To make a bouncy, squashy ride
bonus.reveal: The air squashes and springs back, so bumps don't hurt as much.
